experiment: Exp 33a — spectral pruning on Pythia-410M (scale test)
protocol: same as Exp 32: lmin per head at square point (T=64) + ablation importance (KL) on 6 sampled layers (96 heads)

results.lmin_all_collapsed: 384/384 heads with |lmin| < 1e-5 at the square point

honest_verdict: The spectral criterion does NOT generalize as-is to Pythia-410M: ALL 384 heads are already rank-collapsed at the square point (lmin ~ 0 for everyone), so there is no variance for the criterion to discriminate. This is not a refutation of P1 — it shows Pythia-410M lives DEEPER in the collapse regime than GPT-2 124M (2x the layers, more training). Implication: for models in this regime, head-level pruning via lmin is moot (everything is collapsed); the criterion needs a different operating point (sub-square T) or a different target (pruning whole layers, or the memory-layer decoding of P2).
next: Exp 33b candidates: (1) lmin measured BELOW the square point (T=d_head/2) where pythia still has variance; (2) prune LAYERS by mean lmin (24 layers may discriminate even when heads don't); (3) GPT-2 XL (1.5B, 48 layers) to test the scale direction where GPT-2's variance might persist.
